items.title: Karnataka forms ex-Chief Justice-led panel to review Bidadi Township
items.summary: The Karnataka government has constituted a four-member high-level committee headed by retired High Court judge Justice Guhanathan Narendar to review concerns over the proposed Bidadi Greater Bengaluru Integrated Township project. The committee has been asked to examine various aspects of the project and submit a comprehensive report to the state government within 30 days. The panel also includes retired Chief Secretary SV Ranganath, retired Additional Chief Secretary S R Umashankar and retired IAS officer Prasanna Kumar. The decision comes amid growing opposition from farmers and landowners in villages that are likely to be affected by the proposed township. The government has reiterated that land acquisition for the project will be entirely voluntary and that no landowner will be forced to give up land. The Bidadi township project, located around 40 km from Bengaluru, was first proposed in 2006 but remained stalled for years. The Congress government revived the project with a modified plan, citing growing demand for industrial investment and development around Bengaluru.
